cue: You will hear an interview with a student who organized a screen-free evening.
turns: What gave you the idea for a screen-free evening, Ella?
I saw a similar challenge online, but the idea only felt useful when my friends said we never finished a conversation without looking at our phones. We wanted an evening when we could really talk.
How did the first evening go?

I was worried that nobody would know what to do, so I brought a board game. In fact, we talked for the first hour and only opened the box later. We started too late, though, and some people had to catch the bus home before the game ended.
Yes, but next time we'll start earlier. I don't want everyone to give up their phones all the time. I just want them to notice when their phones get in the way.

cue: You will hear an interview with a student who started a quiet lunch club.
turns: Why did you start the lunch club, Nico?
I used to spend every break finishing homework. After a while I noticed I couldn't concentrate in the afternoon. I wanted a proper break and thought others might need one too.
Was the club popular at first?
Only three people came on the first day. The original room was right by the cafeteria and it was so noisy that we had to move. The library gave us a corner, and after that a lot more people joined.
Will you change anything next month?

Some people want us to add activities every day, but a long list of activities might make it feel like another lesson. I'd rather keep the club relaxed. We can offer games or books and let people choose.
